A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NegMerge and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Renamed and relocated material can be matched reliably despite extensive revision and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP and CIFAR-10 unlearning experiments, sign-conflict analyses, and Grad-CAM examples, alongside explicitly attributed baseline results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds dataset, architecture, forgetting-scenario, sparsity, and model-pool evaluations.

M1.justification: Both versions average task-vector coordinates with unanimously consistent signs and subtract the scaled merged vector from the original model. Equation (1) is algebraically equivalent. Newly documented storage procedures and experimental min/max alternatives do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds CUB-200-2011 and Tiny ImageNet evaluations and CIFAR-10 class-wise forgetting (Tables B8, B9, B13). The original eight CLIP target datasets, ImageNet retain control, and CIFAR-10 remain. Discussion of LLM applicability adds no evaluated language task.

E2.justification: The main unlearning comparator sets remain unchanged. However, the task-vector-addition comparison drops TIES-Merging and MagMax from v1 Table 3 to v2 Table 5. Their continued participation in other experiments does not preserve this particular comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds VGG-16 and Swin-T configurations, a 50% random-forgetting split, and systematic experiments varying pool size and hyperparameter composition (Tables B10–B12, B7, D1–D4). Primary retained settings remain stable. Newly disclosed attention-layer freezing does not establish that the original experiments changed.

E4.justification: New analyses examine pool size and composition, averaging versus minimum/maximum merging, and sparsity across methods, depths, and components (Tables 4, 6, B7, C1–C3, D1–D4). Earlier sign-conflict and task-addition analyses largely remain. The retain-set sensitivity panel and island Grad-CAM example are removed.

E5.justification: Table C3 newly defines and reports variability across layers for component sparsity. Existing three-trial classifier statistics and three-run timing reporting remain unchanged. Table B7 extends the existing mean/standard-deviation convention to a new ablation; it does not establish increased run counts for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and v1 Tables A1–A6, matched to v2 Tables B1–B6, retain their numerical values. Substantial new results cover additional benchmarks and sensitivity analyses. For example, newly evaluated CUB gives average gaps of 7.30 for NegMerge versus 7.41 for Task Arithmetic; class-wise CIFAR-10 gives 3.73 versus 4.18. Some diagnostic result entries are removed.

T1.justification: The core mathematics is unchanged. New Appendix E offers qualitative arguments involving sparsity, linear mode connectivity, and a conjectured stable merged point, but supplies no formal assumptions, derivation, theorem, or proof. Both conclusions acknowledge the absence of theoretical justification.

C1.justification: The central claims about sign-consensual unlearning, knowledge preservation, and computational efficiency persist. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the explicitly claimed validation scope to twelve datasets and four architecture families, including VGG and Swin.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking sparsity to retention, averaging to outlier suppression, and layer depth to knowledge specificity, plus storage and memory arguments. Appendix D.2 qualifies robustness by warning about poorly constructed model pools. Appendices E–F add heuristic mechanism reasoning and prospective applicability beyond image classification.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands documentation with attention-layer freezing, incremental consensus-mask storage, VGG/CUB training settings, and detailed alternative model-pool configurations (Section 3.3; Appendices A and D). These are disclosures and specifications, not evidence of changes to retained experiments. Existing core hyperparameters and the code-access URL remain.

R1.justification: Related work adds focused positioning against Skill Localization, Localize-and-Stitch, and TALL Mask. New representation and linear-mode-connectivity references support added explanations, while some broad pretraining and continual-learning context disappears. The central task-arithmetic/model-merging positioning remains; publication-year updates are not new works.

P1.justification: The introduction, motivation, and method exposition are extensively rewritten and reorganized. Computational cost becomes a separate subsection, implementation details move to Appendix A, and the appendices expand into sections A–F. The title and terminology also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. Figure 1 is redesigned and loses its retain-set panel; Figure 3 loses one example. Numerous new tables are introduced, existing tables are resized or shortened, and retained appendix displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 directly tests the pool-size and composition robustness that v1 largely asserted, and expands standard-classifier validation beyond one dataset, backbone, and forgetting setup. These additions substantially strengthen empirical support for the method's central rationale and applicability. Some diagnostic evidence is trimmed, several new benchmark margins lack uncertainty estimates, and Appendix E remains heuristic, but the broader and more targeted validation provides a clear net improvement.
